a11y.apg: Layout primitive, no role and no keyboard: it is a <div> with CSS grid. Deliberately NOT role="grid" — that is the ARIA pattern for a data grid with cell navigation, which is DataGrid. Same word, different thing.

props.name: children
props.description: Responsive columns with no breakpoints: each one is at least --grid-min wide (15rem by default) and they fill the row, with --space-4 between them.

props.name: gap
props.description: Three steps and no others (ADR-0051): tight is --space-2, normal is --space-4, loose is --space-6. The old rule still holds against ANY spacing; these two extra steps exist for the two measured cases — a note under its value, and a grid of filters.

props.name: min
props.description: The minimum column width. By name (AN-08): xs 8rem, sm 12rem, md 15rem (the default) or lg 20rem — each a number the system already uses (the Gallery tile, the health matrix cell, the Grid default, the xs dialog). Or as a CSS length ("10rem", "155px"), the --grid-min the CSS always read. Until 0.17, "sm" type-checked and collapsed the grid to a single column.

props.name: columns
props.description: A fixed number of equal columns. With it, `min` stops applying. With 12, Grid.Item's `span` gives the 7-of-12 layout of a website page.

props.name: Grid.Item span
props.description: Grid.Item is a grid child that knows how many columns it takes (GAR-03, 06/10/2026). Responsive and mobile-first: span={{base: "12", viewport: {md: "7"}}} takes the whole row on a narrow screen and 7 of 12 from md up. By container too ({base, container: {sm: …}}). Without span, one column, like any grid child.

props.name: className
props.description: Where you set --grid-min for a denser or a wider grid. That variable is the adjustment knob, the same idea as --qr-size on QRCode: a column count as a prop would freeze a number that the container is the one who knows.
